marks.conclusion: A small RL agent on one fixed symmetric maze: ch3 wall, ch0 the agent, ch1 a target/enemy, ch4 items, ch2 empty floor; outputs are five moves in an unknown order.
marks.judge_notes: Score: core A7 B1 C0 D0 E0 = 8, no deductions; bonus 0. Rulings: (1) Border 1: ch3 rows track b1, so always on at wall cells. (2) Channel meanings 2 (ch3 wall, ch0 agent, argued from cell-specific weights). ch1 'goal/target or possibly enemy' is undecided and its chosen story (target) is wrong. ch2 'empty floor' and ch4 'item/food' are reversed against the sheet (ch2 is pellets, ch4 the previous frame). They are offered as 'the most coherent story' with 'can't be ruled out' caveats, so earn nothing and no deduction. (3) Layout 1: maze only. The reply misses that ch2 is absent at the start cell, and gives no placement of the other entities. (4) Depth level 1: it reads first-layer units (29 'south', 21 'west vs east'), dead and constant units, and notes W2 rows track b2, but never follows units to the outputs. (5) Behaviour 0: it says only that features are directional and the task is Pac-Man-like or collect-the-items. (6) Activation 0: 'presumably ReLU'; the dead-unit argument is built on the wrong activation (tanh). Not deducted because 'presumably'. (7) Training 0: 'small reinforcement-learning agent' without evidence tied to RL; it leaves DQN vs PPO open. (8) Name not credited: Pac-Man-like is one possibility among others.
